column3: 1. Integrate [areas within the scope of the updated programme of work] into broader landscape and seascape planning to improve, in accordance with national legislation, biodiversity outcomes, ecological representativeness and connectivity, through participatory and biodiversity-inclusive spatial planning processes, while recognizing and respecting the rights of indigenous peoples and local communities. 1.bis. column3: 2.. Promote the restoration of degraded ecosystems within [areas within the scope of the updated programme of work], and beyond, including buffer zones, ecological corridors, soil biodiversity[, [including] fungal biodiversity,] and inland water ecosystems, with a view to restoring ecological integrity and ecological connectivity across landscapes and seascapes, including through the development of criteria for identifying priority restoration areas and approaches for measuring restoration success, ensuring inclusive and gender-responsive implementation of the restoration efforts, as appropriate. [2.bis Scale up ecological connectivity measures within currently under-represented ecosystems, including marine and island ecosystems, rivers, wetlands, estuaries and coastal zones, and seek, as appropriate, to align terrestrial ecological corridors with riverine and inland water networks, in support of restoring ecological integrity and connectivity across landscapes and seascapes.]
